questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Physics?
options: The study of matter, energy, forces and their interactions
The study of naming living organisms only
The study of business records and accounts
The study of ancient written sources only
questions.correctAnswer: The study of matter, energy, forces and their interactions
questions.explanation: Physics investigates matter, energy, motion, forces and the laws that describe them.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain Physics as a body of knowledge in science.

questions.prompt: Which branch of Physics mainly studies heat and temperature?
questions.explanation: Thermodynamics deals with heat, temperature, energy transfer and related changes in matter.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe branches of Physics as a field of study.

questions.prompt: A learner uses knowledge of forces to design a safer school gate. Which importance of Physics is shown?
options: Solving practical problems in daily life
questions.correctAnswer: Solving practical problems in daily life
questions.explanation: Physics helps people understand forces, materials and motion so they can solve practical design problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Outline the importance of Physics in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which career is most directly linked to Physics after senior school?
questions.explanation: Electrical engineering applies ideas from electricity, magnetism, electronics and measurement.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify possible career opportunities in the field of Physics.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, so its SI unit is the pascal, equal to one newton per square metre.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe pressure as used in Physics.

questions.prompt: A 200 N box rests on an area of 0.5 m2. What pressure does it exert?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = 200 N / 0.5 m2 = 400 Pa.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the relationship between force, area and pressure.

questions.prompt: Which pair of factors directly affects pressure at a point inside a liquid?
options: Colour and smell of the liquid
Width of the room and air temperature only
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure increases with depth, density and gravitational field strength.
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate factors affecting pressure in fluids.

questions.prompt: Calculate the pressure 2 m below water of density 1000 kg/m3 when g = 10 N/kg.
questions.explanation: Using P = density x g x h gives 1000 x 10 x 2 = 20000 Pa.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply P = density x g x h to determine pressure in fluids.

questions.prompt: A hydraulic lift works because pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted in which way?
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle states that pressure in an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally throughout the fluid.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate transmission of pressure in fluids.

questions.prompt: When a learner drinks juice through a straw, what mainly pushes the liquid up the straw?
options: Atmospheric pressure on the juice surface
questions.correctAnswer: Atmospheric pressure on the juice surface
questions.explanation: Sucking lowers pressure inside the straw, so atmospheric pressure on the drink surface pushes liquid upward.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of atmospheric pressure in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Two holes are made on the side of a water tank, one near the top and one near the bottom. Which stream comes out faster?
options: The lower stream, because pressure is greater at greater depth
The upper stream, because it is nearer the air
Both streams, because pressure is independent of depth
Neither stream, because water has no pressure
questions.correctAnswer: The lower stream, because pressure is greater at greater depth
questions.explanation: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth, so the lower hole has a greater pressure difference.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how depth affects pressure in fluids.

questions.prompt: Why does a sharp knife cut sukuma wiki more easily than a blunt knife using the same force?
options: Its smaller contact area produces greater pressure
Its larger contact area reduces pressure
questions.correctAnswer: Its smaller contact area produces greater pressure
questions.explanation: For the same force, reducing the contact area increases pressure on the material being cut.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate pressure to everyday applications involving force and area.

questions.prompt: A school wants taps on a raised water tank to deliver water with greater pressure. Which design change best helps?
options: Place the tank higher above the taps
Paint the tank a brighter colour
Use a wider tank lid only
questions.correctAnswer: Place the tank higher above the taps
questions.explanation: Raising the tank increases the water depth above the taps, which increases pressure at the outlets.
questions.learningOutcome: Use fluid pressure ideas to propose practical water supply solutions.

questions.prompt: What happens to atmospheric pressure as a person climbs from Mombasa towards a high mountain area?
options: It depends only on shoe size
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude because there is less air above the person.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe atmospheric pressure and its effects in nature.

questions.prompt: Which property describes the ability of a material to be drawn into a wire?
questions.explanation: A ductile material can be pulled into a wire without breaking easily.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain mechanical properties of materials.

questions.prompt: According to Hooke's law, extension is directly proportional to which quantity within the elastic limit?
questions.explanation: Within the elastic limit, a spring's extension is proportional to the force applied to it.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate Hooke's law using force and extension.

questions.prompt: A wire of cross-sectional area 0.002 m2 carries a tensile force of 50 N. What is the tensile stress?
questions.explanation: Stress = force/area = 50 / 0.002 = 25000 Pa.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine tensile stress using mathematical formulae.

questions.prompt: A 2.0 m wire extends by 0.01 m. What is its strain?
questions.explanation: Strain = extension/original length = 0.01 / 2.0 = 0.005.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine tensile strain using mathematical formulae.

questions.prompt: A material has stress of 80000 Pa and strain of 0.004. What is its Young's modulus?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus = stress/strain = 80000 / 0.004 = 20000000 Pa.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine modulus of elasticity from stress and strain.

questions.prompt: Which property is most important for a ceramic floor tile that should resist scratching?
questions.explanation: Hardness is resistance to scratching, indentation or wear.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of mechanical properties of materials.

questions.prompt: On a force-extension graph for a spring, what does the end of the straight-line part show?
questions.explanation: The straight-line part shows proportionality between force and extension; beyond it Hooke's law no longer applies.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze force-extension behaviour of elastic materials.

questions.prompt: A footbridge cable must carry large loads and return to its shape after small stretches. Which combination is most suitable?
options: Low hardness and high melting only
questions.explanation: The cable needs strength to resist breaking and elasticity to recover after normal stretching.
questions.learningOutcome: Use material properties to choose materials for specific purposes.

questions.prompt: What does temperature measure?
options: How hot or cold a body is
The total mass of a body
The volume of air around a body
questions.correctAnswer: How hot or cold a body is
questions.explanation: Temperature tells the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of temperature as used in thermal Physics.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is commonly used to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer is designed to measure temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: Measure temperature using different technologies.

questions.prompt: Why are expansion gaps left between sections of a steel bridge?
options: To allow the steel to expand safely when heated
To stop all heat from reaching the bridge
questions.correctAnswer: To allow the steel to expand safely when heated
questions.explanation: Metals expand when heated; gaps prevent buckling or cracking.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of thermal expansion in solids.

questions.prompt: A metal rod of length 2 m has alpha = 0.000012 per degree Celsius. Its temperature rises by 50 degrees Celsius. What is its expansion?
questions.explanation: Expansion = alpha x length x temperature change = 0.000012 x 2 x 50 = 0.0012 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine linear expansion of materials using a mathematical relationship.

questions.prompt: A bimetallic strip bends when heated because the two metals have different what?
questions.explanation: Different metals expand by different amounts for the same temperature rise, causing the strip to bend.
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate thermal expansion in solids and its applications.

questions.prompt: Why can a full glass bottle crack when water inside it freezes?
options: Glass becomes weightless in a freezer
Air pressure inside the freezer becomes zero
questions.explanation: Water has unusual expansion; it expands on freezing, so the ice can exert pressure on the bottle.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain unusual expansion of water and its effects.

questions.prompt: Why is a thermistor useful in an electronic thermometer?
options: Its resistance changes predictably with temperature
It blocks all electric current permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Its resistance changes predictably with temperature
questions.explanation: A thermistor is a temperature-sensitive resistor, so its resistance can be used to infer temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe temperature measurement technologies such as thermistors.

questions.prompt: A clinic needs to check a patient's temperature without touching the skin. Which device is most suitable?
questions.explanation: An infrared thermometer detects thermal radiation from the body surface without contact.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose suitable temperature measurement technologies for real situations.

questions.prompt: What is the moment of a force?
options: The turning effect of a force about a point
The total heat in a body
The pressure inside a liquid only
questions.correctAnswer: The turning effect of a force about a point
questions.explanation: A moment describes how strongly a force tends to rotate a body about a pivot.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine moment of force about a point.

questions.prompt: A 20 N force acts 0.4 m from a pivot at right angles. What is the moment?
questions.explanation: Moment = force x perpendicular distance = 20 x 0.4 = 8 Nm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate moment of a force about a point.

questions.prompt: For a body in rotational equilibrium, which condition must be true?
options: The centre of gravity must disappear
questions.explanation: The principle of moments states that balanced turning effects are equal in opposite directions.
questions.learningOutcome: Verify the principle of moments in turning objects.

questions.prompt: A 10 N load is 0.6 m to the left of a pivot. A balancing force is 0.3 m to the right. What force is needed?
questions.explanation: Balance needs 10 x 0.6 = F x 0.3, so F = 20 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the principle of moments to solve balance problems.

questions.prompt: The centre of gravity of a body is best described as the point where what appears to act?
options: The whole weight of the body
questions.correctAnswer: The whole weight of the body
questions.explanation: The centre of gravity is the point through which the resultant weight of a body acts.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the centre of gravity of regular and irregular objects.

questions.prompt: Why is a bus with heavy luggage on the roof less stable when turning?
options: The centre of gravity is raised
Air pressure inside the bus becomes zero
questions.correctAnswer: The centre of gravity is raised
questions.explanation: A higher centre of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to topple when a turning effect acts.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze factors affecting stability of bodies.

questions.prompt: A couple in mechanics is formed by which arrangement?
options: Two equal parallel forces acting in opposite directions at different points
Two equal forces acting at the same point in the same direction
One force acting through the pivot
No forces acting on a body
questions.correctAnswer: Two equal parallel forces acting in opposite directions at different points
questions.explanation: A couple produces rotation without a resultant force because the forces are equal, opposite and separated.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe torque and couple in turning objects.

questions.prompt: A uniform 4 m plank of weight 100 N rests on supports at both ends. A 200 N learner stands 1 m from the left support. What is the reaction at the right support?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the left support gives right reaction x 4 = 100 x 2 + 200 x 1 = 400, so the reaction is 100 N.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze moment problems involving two points of support.

questions.prompt: Why does a wheelbarrow make carrying soil easier?
options: It acts as a lever and reduces the effort needed
It removes the weight of the soil
questions.correctAnswer: It acts as a lever and reduces the effort needed
questions.explanation: A wheelbarrow uses the wheel as a pivot and provides mechanical advantage to reduce effort.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of moments and stability in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: In Physics, work is done when a force causes what?
options: Displacement in the direction of the force
questions.correctAnswer: Displacement in the direction of the force
questions.explanation: Mechanical work is done when a force moves an object through a distance in the direction of the force.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of work in relation to machines.

questions.prompt: A student pushes a trolley with a force of 30 N through 4 m. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work = force x distance = 30 x 4 = 120 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate work done using force and distance.

questions.prompt: A pump does 600 J of work in 20 s. What is its power?
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = 600 / 20 = 30 W.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate power from work done and time taken.

questions.prompt: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg ball moving at 5 m/s?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = 1/2 x mass x speed squared = 1/2 x 2 x 25 = 25 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine kinetic energy of moving bodies.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg bag is lifted 2 m. If g = 10 N/kg, what is the gain in gravitational potential energy?
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy = mass x g x height = 3 x 10 x 2 = 60 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine gravitational potential energy of raised bodies.

questions.prompt: In a swinging pendulum, energy changes mainly between which two forms?
questions.explanation: As the pendulum moves, height and speed change, so energy transforms between potential and kinetic forms.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate transformation of mechanical energy.

questions.prompt: A machine uses 500 J of input energy and gives 350 J of useful output. What is its efficiency?
questions.explanation: Efficiency = useful output/input x 100% = 350/500 x 100% = 70%.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze efficiency of simple machines.

questions.prompt: Why does an inclined plane help a worker load a heavy drum onto a pickup?
options: It reduces the effort by increasing the distance moved
It makes the drum mass zero
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces the effort by increasing the distance moved
questions.explanation: An inclined plane spreads the work over a longer distance, so a smaller effort can be used.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe how simple machines make work easier.

questions.prompt: A machine has mechanical advantage 4 and velocity ratio 5. What conclusion is best?
questions.explanation: Efficiency = mechanical advantage/velocity ratio x 100% = 4/5 x 100% = 80%.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate performance of simple machines using MA and VR.

questions.prompt: In a first-class lever, where is the pivot placed?
options: Between the effort and the load
questions.correctAnswer: Between the effort and the load
questions.explanation: A first-class lever has the fulcrum between the effort and the load, as in a seesaw.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe types and applications of levers.

questions.prompt: Which formula relates wave speed, frequency and wavelength?
questions.explanation: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain wave properties using basic relationships.

questions.prompt: When light bounces from a plane mirror, which wave property is shown?
questions.explanation: Reflection is the bouncing back of a wave from a surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate reflection of waves.

questions.prompt: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Wave speed = frequency x wavelength = 50 x 2 = 100 m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the wave speed relationship to solve numerical tasks.

questions.prompt: Sound spreading after passing through a doorway is an example of which property?
questions.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading of waves after passing through an opening or around an obstacle.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain diffraction in real-life wave situations.

questions.prompt: Two water waves meet crest to crest. What happens at that point?
options: Constructive interference produces a larger displacement
questions.correctAnswer: Constructive interference produces a larger displacement
questions.explanation: When crests meet, their displacements add to give a larger resultant wave.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze interference of waves qualitatively.

questions.prompt: The formation of a sharp shadow by a small light source shows that light usually travels how?
questions.explanation: Rectilinear propagation means light travels in straight lines in a uniform medium.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain rectilinear propagation of light.

questions.prompt: In a stationary wave on a string, what is a node?
options: A point where the string breaks
A point where sound becomes light
questions.explanation: A node is a fixed point in a stationary wave where the displacement is always zero.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe properties of stationary waves.

questions.prompt: A swing moves with large amplitude when pushed at its natural frequency. What is this effect called?
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when a system is driven at its natural frequency, producing large oscillations.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of stationary waves and resonance.

questions.prompt: Why is modulation used in radio communication?
options: To carry information on a high-frequency carrier wave
To turn radio waves into water waves
To make current flow only in resistors
questions.correctAnswer: To carry information on a high-frequency carrier wave
questions.explanation: Modulation varies a carrier wave so that information such as sound can be transmitted efficiently.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the need for modulation in wave applications.

questions.prompt: An approaching ambulance siren seems higher in pitch than when it moves away. Which effect explains this?
questions.explanation: The Doppler effect is the apparent change in frequency due to relative motion between source and observer.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe Doppler's effect and its applications in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A string fixed at both ends has length 0.5 m and wave speed 100 m/s. What is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, the fundamental frequency is v/(2L) = 100/(2 x 0.5) = 100 Hz.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze numerical relationships in modes of vibration.

questions.prompt: Why does a pencil appear bent when partly dipped in water?
options: Light is refracted at the water-air boundary
questions.correctAnswer: Light is refracted at the water-air boundary
questions.explanation: Refraction changes the direction of light as it passes between water and air.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate refraction of waves in real-life situations.

questions.prompt: What is an isotope?
options: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
A wave reflected from a mirror
A wire with no resistance at room temperature
questions.correctAnswer: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers, so their mass numbers differ.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain terminologies used in radioactivity.

questions.prompt: Which radiation has the lowest penetrating power?
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are stopped by paper or skin because they have low penetrating power.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify types and properties of radioactive emissions.

questions.prompt: What is the charge of a beta-minus particle?
questions.explanation: A beta-minus particle is an electron emitted from an unstable nucleus, so it carries negative charge.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe charge and nature of radioactive emissions.

questions.prompt: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 3 hours. What fraction remains after 6 hours?
questions.explanation: Six hours is two half-lives, so the sample halves twice: 1 to 1/2 to 1/4.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine half-life of radioactive elements using data.

questions.prompt: Which safety practice is best when handling a weak sealed radioactive source in a school demonstration?
options: Use tongs and keep exposure time short
Hold it close to the eye
Keep it in a pocket after class
Open the source to inspect it
questions.correctAnswer: Use tongs and keep exposure time short
questions.explanation: Radiation safety reduces exposure by increasing distance, using shielding and keeping time short.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safety precautions when handling radioactive substances.

questions.prompt: When a nucleus emits an alpha particle, how do its mass number and atomic number change?
options: Mass number decreases by 4 and atomic number decreases by 2
Mass number increases by 4 and atomic number increases by 2
Mass number is unchanged and atomic number decreases by 1
questions.correctAnswer: Mass number decreases by 4 and atomic number decreases by 2
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus with mass number 4 and atomic number 2.
questions.learningOutcome: Illustrate how radionuclides attain stability using nuclear equations.

questions.prompt: Which statement best compares nuclear fission and nuclear fusion?
options: Fission splits heavy nuclei, while fusion joins light nuclei
Fission joins light nuclei, while fusion splits heavy nuclei
Both require electrons to leave a metal wire only
questions.correctAnswer: Fission splits heavy nuclei, while fusion joins light nuclei
questions.explanation: Fission is splitting of a heavy nucleus; fusion is joining of light nuclei, both releasing nuclear energy under suitable conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare nuclear fission, nuclear fusion and their significance.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is commonly used to detect and count ionising radiation?
questions.explanation: A Geiger-Muller tube detects ionising radiation and is used with a counter to measure activity.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate detection of radioactive emissions.

questions.prompt: Which subatomic particle is mainly transferred when objects become charged by rubbing?
questions.explanation: Charging by rubbing usually involves transfer of electrons between materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the origin of charges in a material.

questions.prompt: What happens between two like electric charges?
questions.explanation: The basic law of electrostatics states that like charges repel and unlike charges attract.
questions.learningOutcome: State the law of electrostatics.

questions.prompt: A plastic ruler rubbed with dry hair attracts small paper pieces. What caused this attraction?
questions.explanation: Rubbing transfers charge to the ruler, and the charged ruler attracts neutral paper by electrostatic induction.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe generation of static charges on bodies.

questions.prompt: In charging by induction, why can a conductor become charged without direct contact with the charged rod?
options: Charges inside the conductor are redistributed and then separated by earthing
The conductor changes into a magnet only
The rod melts into the conductor
questions.correctAnswer: Charges inside the conductor are redistributed and then separated by earthing
questions.explanation: Induction uses charge redistribution due to a nearby charged body and earthing to leave net charge on the conductor.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe methods of charging a conductor.

questions.prompt: What is one use of a leaf electroscope?
options: Testing whether a body is charged
Measuring the depth of a lake
questions.correctAnswer: Testing whether a body is charged
questions.explanation: A leaf electroscope can show the presence and sometimes the type of electric charge.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain uses of an electroscope.

questions.prompt: Where is charge most concentrated on a pear-shaped metal conductor?
questions.explanation: Charge density is greatest at sharp points on conductors, producing a stronger electric field there.
questions.learningOutcome: Illustrate charge distribution on conductors of various shapes.

questions.prompt: How does a lightning arrestor protect a tall building?
options: It provides a low-resistance path for charge to the ground
It stores lightning inside the walls
It turns lightning into sound only
questions.correctAnswer: It provides a low-resistance path for charge to the ground
questions.explanation: A lightning arrestor safely conducts charge to earth, reducing damage to the building.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe applications of electrostatic charges and lightning safety.

questions.prompt: Why is a pointed conductor more effective than a rounded one at discharging into air?
options: Its high charge density creates a stronger electric field near the point
It is always hotter than a rounded conductor
questions.correctAnswer: Its high charge density creates a stronger electric field near the point
questions.explanation: A sharp point concentrates charge, which can ionise nearby air more easily and allow discharge.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze charge distribution and electric field effects on conductors.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain terminologies used in current electricity.

questions.prompt: How should an ammeter be connected to measure current through a lamp?
options: In parallel with the battery only
questions.explanation: An ammeter must be in series so the same current passing through the lamp passes through the meter.
questions.learningOutcome: Measure current in an electric circuit.

questions.prompt: Which equation represents Ohm's law for an ohmic conductor?
options: P = density x g x h
questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that potential difference equals current multiplied by resistance for an ohmic conductor at constant temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: Verify the relationship V = IR in current electricity.

questions.prompt: A resistor has 12 V across it and current 3 A through it. What is its resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance = voltage/current = 12 / 3 = 4 ohms.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine resistance using voltage and current.

questions.prompt: Two resistors of 3 ohms and 5 ohms are connected in series. What is their effective resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistances in series add directly: 3 + 5 = 8 ohms.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine effective resistance of series resistor networks.

questions.prompt: Two equal resistors of 6 ohms each are connected in parallel. What is their effective resistance?
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel, the effective resistance is half of one resistor, so it is 3 ohms.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine effective resistance of parallel resistor networks.

questions.prompt: A cell of emf 6 V has internal resistance 1 ohm and supplies current 2 A. What terminal voltage is delivered to the external circuit?
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage = emf - current x internal resistance = 6 - 2 x 1 = 4 V.
questions.learningOutcome: Use E = I(R + r) and related ideas in current electricity.

questions.prompt: A wire's resistance increases when its length increases because resistance is proportional to what?
options: Number of lamps in the room only
questions.explanation: For the same material and area, resistance is directly proportional to conductor length.
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate factors affecting resistance of ohmic conductors.

questions.prompt: A resistor has colour bands red, violet, brown and gold. What resistance value does this show?
questions.explanation: Red is 2, violet is 7, and brown is a multiplier of 10, giving 27 x 10 = 270 ohms.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine resistance using resistor colour codes.

questions.prompt: An electric iron operates at 240 V and draws 5 A. What power does it use?
questions.explanation: Electrical power = voltage x current = 240 x 5 = 1200 W.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the relationship of potential difference and current to power.

questions.prompt: A 4 ohm resistor is in series with two 6 ohm resistors connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: The two 6 ohm resistors in parallel give 3 ohms; adding the series 4 ohms gives 7 ohms.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze mixed resistor networks.

questions.prompt: Why is a filament lamp described as non-ohmic?
options: Its resistance changes as temperature rises
It has no current at any voltage
It obeys V = IR perfectly at all temperatures
questions.correctAnswer: Its resistance changes as temperature rises
questions.explanation: As the filament heats up, its resistance changes, so the current-voltage graph is not a straight line.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify conductors as ohmic or non-ohmic using current-voltage behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which material type has electrical conductivity between conductors and insulators?
questions.explanation: A semiconductor conducts better than an insulator but not as well as a good conductor under normal conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of conductor, insulator, semiconductor and superconductor.

questions.prompt: In energy band theory, why is a good conductor able to carry current easily?
options: It has many electrons available to move into nearby empty states
It has no electrons at all
Its band gap is always larger than that of an insulator
Its protons move freely through the wire
questions.correctAnswer: It has many electrons available to move into nearby empty states
questions.explanation: Conductors have available energy states that allow electrons to move easily when a potential difference is applied.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish conductors, semiconductors and insulators using energy band theory.

questions.prompt: What is an intrinsic semiconductor?
options: A pure semiconductor with no deliberate impurity added
A metal wire with zero resistance at all temperatures
A plastic that never changes resistance
A battery with internal resistance only
questions.correctAnswer: A pure semiconductor with no deliberate impurity added
questions.explanation: An intrinsic semiconductor is pure, while extrinsic semiconductors are doped with impurities.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors.

questions.prompt: An n-type semiconductor is formed by doping silicon with an impurity that provides extra what?
questions.explanation: N-type doping adds donor atoms that provide extra electrons as majority charge carriers.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain formation of n-type and p-type semiconductors.

questions.prompt: How does increasing temperature usually affect a pure semiconductor?
options: It increases the number of charge carriers and lowers resistance
It makes it behave exactly like an ideal insulator
It changes it into a liquid metal immediately
questions.correctAnswer: It increases the number of charge carriers and lowers resistance
questions.explanation: Heating gives more electrons enough energy to cross the band gap, increasing conductivity.
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate electrical behaviour of semiconductors with varying temperature.

questions.prompt: What is the greenhouse effect?
options: Warming caused when some gases trap outgoing infrared radiation
Cooling caused by removing all air from Earth
The reflection of sound by mountains
questions.correctAnswer: Warming caused when some gases trap outgoing infrared radiation
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, helping warm the lower atmosphere.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes ozone layer protection from the greenhouse effect?
options: The ozone layer absorbs much ultraviolet radiation, while greenhouse gases trap infrared radiation
The ozone layer is the same as carbon dioxide
The greenhouse effect blocks all sunlight from reaching Earth
Ozone depletion directly makes gravity stronger
questions.correctAnswer: The ozone layer absorbs much ultraviolet radiation, while greenhouse gases trap infrared radiation
questions.explanation: Ozone high in the atmosphere reduces harmful ultraviolet radiation, while greenhouse gases affect heat radiation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of the ozone layer in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which action best helps a school reduce its contribution to climate change?
options: Use energy-efficient lighting and plant trees around the compound
Leave unused lights on every night
Remove all vegetation to make bare ground
questions.correctAnswer: Use energy-efficient lighting and plant trees around the compound
questions.explanation: Saving energy reduces emissions, and trees absorb carbon dioxide while improving the local environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe mitigating factors against climate change in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which theory explains the origin of the universe from a very hot, dense early state?
questions.explanation: The Big Bang theory describes the universe expanding from a very hot and dense early state.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the Big Bang theory of the origin of the universe.

questions.prompt: Which item is a natural satellite?
questions.explanation: A natural satellite is a natural body that orbits a planet; the Moon orbits Earth.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify celestial bodies in the universe.

questions.prompt: Why is a telescope important in space physics?
options: It collects and focuses radiation from distant celestial bodies
It measures electric current in a circuit only
questions.correctAnswer: It collects and focuses radiation from distant celestial bodies
questions.explanation: Telescopes gather radiation such as visible light or radio waves, making distant objects easier to observe and study.
